title: RFID Cable Seal Tag — Tamper-Evident Bonded Cargo
summary: In real-world deployments, RFID cable seal tags combine a tamper-evident galvanized or stainless steel cable lock with an embedded UHF RFID chip — giving shipping containers, truck trailers, bonded-cargo holds, utility meter enclosures and high-value shipments both a physical indicative / high-security seal under ISO 17712 and a real-time digital chain-of-custody identity under ISO 18185 e-Seal data. Once threaded and locked, the cable cannot be reopened without visible destruction; the UHF chip is read at 2–4 m by portal readers at yard gates, port terminals and border checkpoints, and the factory-programmed TID defeats seal-substitution and clone-and-swap fraud. Aligned with CBP C-TPAT, WCO SAFE Framework, EU AEO, CBSA PIP, ABF ATT and the ongoing CBP e-Seal advance-electronic-cargo-information pilot.

heroPoints: Tamper-evident steel cable. Once locked, the seal cannot be opened without visible destruction — provides ISO 17712 Indicative and (thick-cable variant) ISO 17712 High Security evidence of unauthorized access.

Embedded UHF RAIN RFID chip. Enables 2–4 m automated reads at yard gates, dock doors and border checkpoints without manual barcode scanning — aligned with ISO 18185 e-Seal data frames and the CBP e-Seal pilot.

Unique TID + printed serial + QR code. Three-factor identity ties the physical seal to the digital record, preventing seal cloning, substitution and counterfeit attacks in C-TPAT / AEO / CBSA PIP / ABF ATT programmes.

sections.title: Why mechanical-only seals and manual logging fail C-TPAT / WCO SAFE / AEO programmes
bullets: Traditional bolt seals and padlock seals provide physical tamper evidence but carry no digital identity. Seal numbers must be manually recorded at each custody transfer point — data-entry errors affect 3–8 % of shipments and break chain-of-custody documentation needed for C-TPAT and AEO trusted-trader programmes.

Barcode-printed cable seals require line-of-sight scanning at close range, slowing truck-gate processing to 45–90 s per vehicle as drivers exit the cab to present the seal. At a container yard or port terminal handling 1,000+ trucks/day, barcode-only seals force labor or wait-time proportional to fleet size.

Manual seal verification at container yards handles 200–400 containers per shift. Scaling to 1,000+ containers per day requires proportional headcount growth and erodes logistics margins — or alternatively creates verification gaps that break C-TPAT Tier II / III minimum criteria.

Seal-cloning and substitution fraud: criminals remove a genuine seal, access the cargo, and apply a counterfeit seal with a matching printed serial number. Without a cryptographic digital identity (unclonable TID), the substitution is undetectable until the shipment reaches its destination.

Customs and border agencies increasingly require electronic seal data (e-Seal) for expedited clearance — CBP e-Seal pilots, EU Single Window, ABF ATT, CBSA PIP and the WCO SAFE Framework all reference ISO 18185 e-Seal data structures. Paper-based seal logs do not qualify for expedited clearance status.

sections.title: How Proud Tek RFID cable seal tags secure the C-TPAT / WCO SAFE supply chain
bullets: 1.8 mm galvanized or 316 stainless steel cable threads through ISO 668 container door hasps, trailer-door handles, meter rings and cargo tie-down points. The self-locking aluminum-alloy body engages with an audible click and cannot be reversed without cutting the cable, which leaves visible tamper evidence per ISO 17712 Indicative criteria.

{chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:name} or {chip:nxp-ucode-9:name} UHF chip embedded in the seal body provides 2–4 m read range at 860–960 MHz — enabling automated gate reads as trucks pass through RFID-equipped portals at 15–20 km/h without stopping. ISO 18185 e-Seal data frames are supported as an option for customs-single-window integration.

Each seal carries a factory-programmed unique TID (read-only, unclonable) plus a laser-printed serial number on the seal body and an optional QR code. The receiving party verifies that the RFID TID matches the expected digital record stored in the shipper's TMS and the WCO SAFE unique consignment reference (UCR), defeating seal-substitution fraud.

96–128-bit user-writable EPC memory stores container number, shipper code, route ID, sealing timestamp, WCO SAFE UCR and optional e-Seal frame. Written at the sealing point and verified at each custody transfer portal read.

Operating temperature −40 °C to +80 °C and IP67 ingress rating. Suitable for refrigerated containers, tropical shipping routes, open-top rail transport, multi-month ocean voyages and saltwater-exposed port-terminal environments.

sections.title: Applications across ocean, road, rail, bonded-warehouse and utility-meter use cases
bullets: Ocean container shipping: seal ISO 668 containers at the shipper's CFS and verify integrity at every transshipment port, rail terminal and final destination gate — feeding C-TPAT / AEO / PIP advance-electronic-cargo data.
Truck and trailer security: secure trailer rear-door hasps at the loading dock and verify at weigh stations, border crossings and delivery sites via RFID portal reads.
Rail intermodal: seal COFC / TOFC container doors and rail-car cross-slide doors for through-chain reads at rail terminals (Class I / short-line).
Bonded-warehouse / in-transit: seal bonded cargo moving between Foreign-Trade Zones / bonded facilities — providing the electronic seal data required for expedited customs clearance under WCO SAFE.
Utility meter tamper detection: seal electric, gas and water meter enclosures to detect unauthorized access, meter tampering and revenue-protection cases.
High-value cargo: pharmaceuticals, electronics, tobacco and spirits shipments requiring documented chain-of-custody for insurance, regulatory (FDA DSCSA, TTB) and anti-theft programmes.

sections.title: Integration with TMS, customs single-window and AEO / C-TPAT programmes
bullets: Sealing point: at shipper dock, operator applies the seal, reads the TID / EPC and pairs it with the WCO SAFE UCR in the TMS — creating the master chain-of-custody record.
Portal gate reader: yard-gate, port-terminal and border-checkpoint portal readers capture EPC and TID. Cross-check against expected value; any mismatch flags seal substitution.
Handheld verification: bonded-warehouse and delivery-site staff verify seal intact + TID match before cargo release.
Customs single-window: ISO 18185 e-Seal frame feeds the customs advance-electronic-cargo-information system (CBP, CBSA, EU, ABF).
Audit + compliance: full event chain (sealing, every portal read, receiving verification) is retained for C-TPAT / AEO / PIP audit — replacing paper seal logs.

items.label: Weeks 0–3 — lane selection + data model
items.text: Choose a pilot export lane (e.g. single US→EU or US→CN route). Define the e-Seal data model (WCO SAFE UCR, EPC payload, TID verify procedure). Align with existing TMS / customs broker integration.

items.label: Weeks 3–8 — sealing-terminal deployment
items.text: Install sealing terminals at shipper dock(s). Train operators on one-click seal-apply + TID-read procedure. Integrate event capture into TMS.

items.label: Weeks 8–14 — portal reader rollout at custody transfer points
items.text: Deploy portal readers at origin port gate, destination port gate and key border crossings. Validate TID verify sub-100 ms performance.

items.label: Weeks 14–24 — customs single-window + C-TPAT / AEO certification
items.text: Programme experience across C-TPAT / AEO / PIP e-seal contributes the audit, refresh and onboarding patterns that inform this solution's operating playbook. wire ISO 18185 e-Seal frame into customs single-window and file trusted-trader tier upgrade with CBP, CBSA, EU customs or ABF based on validated chain-of-custody evidence.

faq.question: Does the RFID cable seal meet ISO 17712 for container security?
faq.answer: The RFID cable seal is designed to meet ISO 17712 Indicative seal requirements — the steel cable resists casual tampering and any forced removal leaves visible evidence of breach. For high-security applications requiring ISO 17712 'H' (High Security) classification needed for C-TPAT Tier III and AEO-S programmes, we offer a thicker-shackle bolt-seal variant. Specify your compliance target (Indicative vs. High Security) when ordering.

faq.question: Can the RFID chip in the seal be cloned?
faq.answer: No. Each chip carries a factory-programmed TID (Tag Identifier) that is burned into silicon at manufacturing and cannot be re-written or duplicated. At the sealing point, the TID is recorded in your logistics system alongside the WCO SAFE UCR. At the receiving end, the reader verifies the TID against the expected record in sub-100 ms; any mismatch flags a potential seal substitution before cargo release.

faq.question: Does the seal support ISO 18185 e-Seal data for CBP / CBSA / AEO expedited clearance?
faq.answer: Yes. The ISO 18185 e-Seal data-frame option is programmable into the user memory and exposed through the RFID read event. Customs broker integrations can feed the e-Seal frame directly into the CBP ACE / CBSA EDI / EU Customs single-window / ABF ICS portals — qualifying the shipment for C-TPAT / AEO / PIP / ATT expedited processing lanes.
